title: The World's Highest Train Pumps Oxygen Into the Cabin — Road to Tibet | China Travel Expert
description:
There's a train in China that climbs so high it pumps extra oxygen into the carriage so passengers can breathe.

The Qinghai–Tibet Railway is the highest railway on Earth. From Xining it runs up to Lhasa, cresting Tanggula Pass at 5,072 meters — where the outside air holds only about half the oxygen you're used to. So the sealed carriages are enriched to about 23.5% oxygen, with a personal oxygen port at every seat. The climb takes a full day and night across the Tibetan plateau.

🧭 Expert Tip: Foreign travelers can't board solo — you need a Tibet Travel Permit, arranged in advance through a licensed travel agency on a guided tour. Check official sources before you plan, as rules change.
